 Judgment

1. The present appeal is filed by the State challenging the judgment and award passed by the learned Reference Court dated 30.04.2010 in Land Acquisition Reference No.659 of 1999, arising from the common judgment and award passed by the learned Reference Court in LRC Nos.652 to 667 of Special Land Acquisition Officer vs Bharatsinh Kesarisinh on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47254196/
1 1999.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2. At the outset, it is submitted by the learned AGP Mr. Patel that the present appeal is arising from the same award, which NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4473/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined was the subject matter of challenge before this Court in First Appeal No.443 of 2026,
where this Court has dismissed the appeal on merits.
3. Having considered the submissions made by the learned AGP Mr. Patel, this Court referred to the decision dated 26.02.2026 passed in First Appeal No.443 of 2026, which is reproduced hereinbelow.

"This appeal is preferred under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, read with Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, assailing the judgment and order dated 30.04.2010 passed by the learned Reference Court in LAR No. 652 of 1999,
consolidated with LAR Nos. 652 of 1999 to 667 of 1999, whereby the learned Reference Court has determined additional compensation at the rate of Rs. 37/- per square metre for the land situated in Village Karmali, Taluka District Bharuch,
acquired for the purpose of construction of the Shukla Tirth Branch Distributory Canal under the Narmada Project.

2. The case of the appellant is that, in respect of the said branch, the notification under Section 4 of the Act was published in the Official Gazette on 28.08.1997, and the notification under Section 6 was published on 21.05.1998.

The learned Special Land Acquisition Officer, thereafter, passed an award under Section 11 dated 22.02.1999, awarding Rs. 600/- per Are, which was challenged before the learned Reference Court by filing an application under NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4473/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined Section 18 of the Act, claiming additional compensation for the acquired land.

The learned Reference Court, relying on the decision rendered in LAR No. 1710 of 1998, in which the Section 4 notification dated 07.02.1996 was considered, determined the market value, which is impugned in the present appeal.

3. Heard learned AGP Mr. Parth Patel for the State.
4.
Learned AGP, Mr. Patel, contended that the learned Reference Court erred in granting 15% escalation in the market value, relying on the decision in LAR No. 1710 of 1998.
It was submitted that, as the village in question is situated in the interior of Taluka Bharuch, a reasonable escalation would have been around 7.5% per annum instead of 15%.
Learned AGP submitted that by granting 15% escalation, the learned Reference Court committed an error, and therefore, the impugned judgment deserves interference.

5. Upon considering the submissions of the learned AGP and perusing the reasons assigned by the learned Reference Court, it is observed that while determining the Special Land Acquisition Officer vs Bharatsinh Kesarisinh on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47254196/
2 market value of the land under acquisition, reliance was placed on the decision in LAR No. 1710 of 1998.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As noted, no appeal has been filed by the State against that decision.

It is further observed that the said decision pertained to land situated in the same village, viz., Karmali, for which the Section 4 notification was dated 07.02.1996,
whereas in the present case, the notification is dated 28.08.1997, i.e., 18 months later.

In view of the time difference of one and a half years, the learned Reference Court granted price escalation at the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4473/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined rate of 15%, which, in the opinion of this Court, is just and reasonable.

5.1. So far as the contention regarding deduction on account of price escalation being less than 10% is concerned, apart from merely asserting that the land situated in Village Karmali, which is under acquisition, is located at a considerable distance from Taluka Bharuch, no substantive material has been placed on record.

When the appellant contends that the acquired land is situated in an interior village as compared to the city area, it is incumbent upon the appellant to demonstrate before this Court the nature of amenities available in the said village and the deficiencies, if any, so as to justify a price escalation rate lower than 10% per year.
In the absence of any such evidence to substantiate the said contention, this Court does not find any justifiable ground to interfere with the impugned judgment.
6. Resultantly, the appeal is dismissed."
4. Considering the above background, the First Appeal does not deserve to be entertained and is dismissed.
ORDER IN CIVIL APPLICATION (FOR STAY) NO. 1 of 2022
In view of the order passed in the main matter, the connected civil application does not survive and the same stands disposed of accordingly.
